claims.text: The starting material is as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
The intervention applies 10–15% plastic pre-strain followed by a short annealing treatment.
The pre-strain and annealing treatment will produce nanoscale secondary-phase precipitates in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The pre-strain and annealing treatment will refine the grain structure of HfZrTiTa0.53.
Nano-precipitates and refined grain boundaries will impede dislocation motion.
Nano-precipitates and refined grain boundaries will provide additional kinematic hardening.
The induced microstructure will interrupt the formation of continuous shear bands.
The refined microstructure will increase dislocation storage and strain hardening, thereby making deformation more homogeneous.
High-rate compressive loading has produced a clustering-to-ordering transition in another high-entropy alloy system.
Clustering-to-ordering transitions cause premature strain localization and impact-induced energy release.
The proposed treatment will disrupt clustering-to-ordering transitions in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed treatment will delay thermo-plastic instability under adiabatic loading.
The treated alloy will have approximately 15–20% higher yield strength than the baseline alloy.
The treated alloy will have higher compressive strength than the baseline alloy.
The treated alloy will exhibit greater uniform deformation, higher fracture strain, and improved resistance to shear localization.
The treated alloy will exhibit a lower and less abrupt impact-induced energy release than the baseline alloy.
The predicted improvements apply to adiabatic dynamic compression at strain rates of 10^3–10^4 s^-1 and may weaken or disappear at lower rates or under non-adiabatic conditions.
